newsitem.title: VATICAN: Convalescing Pope only able to give brief speech.
newsitem.headline: Convalescing Pope only able to give brief speech.

text.p: Pope John Paul, apparently not yet strong enough following surgery to hold a general audience, on Wednesday read brief greetings instead to pilgrims in St Peter's Square.
Vatican officials said earlier this month the Pope had hoped to resume his 90-minute weekly general audiences on Wednesday, but announced on Tuesday he would not hold this week's.

Officials said this was partly to allow the Pope to continue resting and partly because the Vatican audience hall is undergoing preparation for a concert in the Pope's honour on Thursday night. He is not due to attend the concert.

The Pope instead addressed pilgrims and tourists for just under 15 minutes from the window of his private apartments overlooking the square. He spoke in a relatively strong voice, using eight languages.
The 76-year-old Polish Pope is on a reduced schedule following surgery on October 8 to remove an inflamed appendix that had caused several bouts of fever.

He resumed pastoral activities last Sunday when he participated in the first part of a Byzantine Rite mass in St Peter's Basilica and is due to be the lead celebrant at a mass there to mark the Roman Catholic feast of All Saints on Friday.
The feast is particularly significant this year because it coincides with the 50th anniversary of the Pope's ordination as a priest in his native Poland.
The Pope mentioned the anniversary in his brief address to pilgrims on Wednesday and also said he was following events in Zaire with deep worry.
He branded ethnic strife "shameful" and called for a negotiated solution to the problems of a widening conflict in central Africa.
